behavioral_evidence.value: Directed item-transition log-odds (a behaviour-conditioned pair weight), computed over consecutive items of TRAIN sequences and restricted at use time to pairs whose two endpoints are both in the current batch.

behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: One pass over TRAIN sequences only: n_ij = number of consecutive (i->j) transitions, n_i = sum_j n_ij, T = sum_ij n_ij; then b_ij = clip(log(n_ij*T/(n_i*n_j)), 0, log T)/log T, so 0 means 'no more than chance' (threshold at independence) and 1 means 'maximally over-represented'. Stored as a sparse train-item x train-item table, together with the per-epoch hard SID buffer khat^{prev}_{l,i} produced by forward passes over TRAIN items only.

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak
behavioral_evidence.value: The transition counts, the b_ij table and the occupancy buffer are built exclusively from TRAIN sequences and TRAIN items; validation interactions are used only after an epoch to log diagnostics and never to build codes, curvatures, gamma_l, R_bar or b_ij; no test interaction of any kind enters SID construction. Cold items get zero rows in b_ij and are quantized by the curved distance alone, so validation or test co-occurrence cannot be smuggled into a prefix.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: The same code path with Ab_l forced to zero (or the behaviour weight alpha_l set to 0) so the cost is the tapered curved distance alone inside the same balanced Sinkhorn: no successor affinity, no signed suffix term, prefixes no longer behaviour-predictive and the suffix no longer dispersive. Present and exercised in unit tests, not trained.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The single formal run: tapered Poincare curvature per level (kappa_l = u1^2/(s_1*s_l)) plus the signed per-pair behaviour term plus balanced curved Sinkhorn dispatch, straight-through preserved, 3000 Stage-2 epochs on four cards, then the frozen Stage-3 protocol, one seed, no early stopping.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: The same code path with kappa_l -> 0 in every map and distance (exp_0 becomes the identity, d becomes the Euclidean distance) and the codewords used directly, with the behaviour term, the sign schedule, alpha_l and the Sinkhorn unchanged: this is the Euclidean quantiser with behaviour only. Present and unit-tested, not trained.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training split only: one pass over training sequences before Stage-2 training builds sparse counts N(i,j) over consecutive pairs within a session, row-normalised with epsilon smoothing to T; succ(i) is cached once. During Stage 2, at the end of every epoch, the level-l hard codes of all 24556 training items are tallied from the epoch's own forward passes, and Ab_l is rebuilt as the row-normalised 256x256 matrix of transition mass from code k to the code containing succ(i); no validation or test interaction is ever read.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed training-only item transitions aggregated to a per-pair code affinity: T(i,j) = row-normalised count of consecutive (i -> j) pairs inside training-split sequences, reduced per epoch to Ab_l[k,k'] = transition mass from level-l code k to the level-l code of the successor, plus the single cached successor succ(i) = argmax_j T(i,j).
ideas.cost_estimate: Per step at the frozen scale: the Poincare distance matrix is unchanged in size (L*B*K = 3*1023*256 = 786k distances, each exp/artanh, already present in the curved baseline); new cost is the Sinkhorn, 30 alternating normalisations over three B x K matrices = 30*3*1023*256 ~ 23.6M elementwise/reduction ops, a few percent of one transformer step, plus one 1023x256 fp32 buffer per level (~1 MB each). Per epoch the behaviour statistics (h_l over 24556 items, succ cached once, Ab_l 256x256 accumulations) are accumulated from the existing forward passes with no extra forward, so ~1-2 ms per epoch. Overall wall clock +10 to 18% over the baseline for 3000 epochs on four cards, memory +~5%, no extra data pass, no extra training run.
ideas.coupling_equation: M_l[i,k] = d_{kappa_l}( exp_0^{kappa_l}(r_l(i)), exp_0^{kappa_l}(E_l[k]) )^2 / s_l^2  -  alpha_l * sigma_l * Ab_l[ k , h_l(succ(i)) ],  with kappa_l = u1^2/(s_1*s_l), alpha_l = std_batch(C_l)/std_batch(B_l), sigma_l = +1 (l<L), -1 (l=L), hard_l(i) = argmax_k Sinkhorn_{T=1}(M_l)[i,k].
ideas.coupling_path: One score, two divisors of the same decision: M_l[i,k] = C_l[i,k] - alpha_l*sigma_l*B_l[i,k], where C_l is the tapered curved distance and B_l is the per-pair behaviour affinity of code k with the level-l code of the item's top training successor; the sign is +1 for levels 1-2 and -1 for level 3. M_l feeds the balanced Sinkhorn whose argmax produces the SID digit and whose straight-through gather selects the same codeword positions used by the decoder. Setting the behaviour matrix to zero removes B_l and changes every digit; replacing d_{kappa_l} by the Euclidean distance (kappa_l -> 0) changes C_l and the codeword placement and therefore changes every digit; neither arm exists without the other inside the same score.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: The coupling is worth keeping only if, in the single coupled run, level-3 occupancy stops collapsing (l3_collision below the 0.35 admission gate, i.e. clearly under the 0.549 Euclidean baseline and far under the 0.943 OCCURV value) while the first-order gain survives (valid_l1_hard_er <= 4 and positive_hit_rate >= 0.12) and level-2 prefix diversity stays large (level2_distinct_prefixes in the thousands, not hundreds). If those hold and Stage3 test Recall@10 exceeds 0.065 (baseline 0.0555, best 0.0638), the mechanism is confirmed; if the taper preserves ER but l3_collision stays above 0.35, the saturation diagnosis is wrong; if l3_collision falls but ER regresses to baseline scale, the balanced dispatch is destroying the curvature gain and the suffix-level sign inversion is not the right dispersion device.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the residual-quantiser assignment and codebook placement: every level's assignment cost is a Poincare squared distance at that level's curvature, the codeword positions c_{l,k} = exp_0^{kappa_l}(E_l[k]) are produced by the same map from the tangent parameters that the decoder consumes, and the curvature used for a level is recomputed each step from the measured residual scale of that level.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball model of constant negative curvature -kappa_l, exponential map exp_0^{kappa_l}(v) = tanh(sqrt(kappa_l)*||v||)/(sqrt(kappa_l)*||v||) * v (and its inverse log_0), Poincare distance d_{kappa_l}(u,v) = (2/sqrt(kappa_l)) * artanh(sqrt(kappa_l)*||(-u) xor v||), with the per-level curvature kappa_l = u1^2/(s_1*s_l), u1 = 0.5, s_l = EMA of the RMS of the level-l tangent residual, so the load u_l = sqrt(kappa_l)*s_l = u1*sqrt(s_l/s_1) is <= 0.5 and strictly decreasing with depth.
ideas.key_change: The residual quantiser's assignment cost becomes a per-level curved cost whose curvature is re-derived every step from a measured residual scale, with a signed per-pair behaviour term added inside that cost, rescaled by a batch-derived weight and dispatched by log-domain balanced Sinkhorn; codeword positions used in reconstruction are the same points produced by the same exp map at the same per-level curvature, and the straight-through estimator is kept on the Sinkhorn soft assignment.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Every behaviour quantity is a function of training-split sequence pairs and of model-internal quantities (residuals, hard code ids) of the training items only. succ(i), T and Ab_l are built before or during Stage-2 training from the training split; they are frozen and reused at validation/test time and are never recomputed from validation or test sequences. The curvature schedule uses s_l, an EMA of training-batch residual RMS. Validation is used only to record diagnostics (which are never admission gates) and test only for the final Recall@10, so no validation or test interaction can enter SID construction.
ideas.motivation: Uniform-strength curvature reproduced the measured first-order gain (hard Euclidean assignment error 16.39 -> 2.49/3.89, positive-hit 0.079 -> 0.12-0.26) but collapsed the third level (l3_collision 0.55-1.00, only 784 level-2 distinct prefixes in the OCCURV arm), and every such arm was rejected by the 35% gate. The geometric cause is that with one curvature magnitude and shrinking deep residuals r_l, the hyperbolic load u_l = sqrt(kappa_l)*s_l stays large, the level-3 residuals are pushed toward the ball boundary where Poincare distances saturate, and the argmin returns the same code for nearly every item. The behavioural cause is that a purely attractive behaviour term lets the suffix code copy the dominant successor suffix. The idea fixes the first by a curvature schedule whose load decays with the measured residual scale and the second by inverting the sign of the same per-pair behaviour affinity at the last level, with balanced dispatch so no single code can absorb the batch.
ideas.novelty: Not a uniform curvature field (OCCURV-FIELD), not popularity-sized capacity cells (GEOCAP), not two-leg parallel transport (holonomy-path-behaviour-rq). Three elements are new here: (1) a per-level curvature kappa_l = u1^2/(s_1*s_l) whose hyperbolic load u_l = u1*sqrt(s_l/s_1) is DERIVED from the measured per-level residual RMS, so curvature effect is strong at level 1 and decays at level 3 and the ball is never approached near its boundary (tanh(u_l) <= tanh(0.5) always); (2) the SAME per-pair behaviour affinity matrix enters with OPPOSITE sign per level (+ attraction at prefix levels 1-2, - repulsion at suffix level 3), making the prefix behaviour-predictive and the suffix an innovation digit that cannot copy the successor's suffix code; (3) the assignment is a balanced curved Sinkhorn whose cost is curvature-conditioned, so code occupancy at level 3 is bounded by construction instead of by a repulsion loss.
ideas.observables: Recorded per epoch and at the end of the single run: per-level residual RMS s_l and curvature kappa_l with the load u_l = sqrt(kappa_l)*s_l (must stay <= 0.5 and decrease from level 1 to level 3), level-3 code occupancy histogram and l3_collision (target below the 0.35 gate, clearly under the 0.549 Euclidean baseline), level2_distinct_prefixes (thousands, not hundreds), valid_l1_hard_er and positive_hit_rate on the validation split (hard ER <= 4, positive-hit >= 0.12), prefix behaviour predictability (fraction of items whose training successor shares the level-1-2 prefix), Sinkhorn marginal residual per level as a numerical health check, and finally Stage3 test Recall@10, which must exceed 0.065.
risks: Per-batch balanced dispatch is computed on ~1023 items and 256 codes (~4 items per code), so the training assignment is batch-dependent; argmin at evaluation may not reproduce the balanced occupancy and l3_collision could come back above the gate.; The suffix-level negative behaviour term fights the generative objective: if the Stage-3 generator relies on the last digit being correlated with the successor's last digit, recall can drop even though occupancy spreads.; The curvature schedule depends on an EMA of residual RMS; early in training the estimate is noisy, kappa_l can swing, and the level-1 separation gain seen in GEOCAP/OCCURV may be delayed or lost in the first few hundred epochs (no early stopping is allowed, so a bad transient is paid for).; When the level-3 code map is already collapsed, h_3(succ(i)) is nearly constant, so the signed behaviour term is nearly constant across k and does nothing; only the Sinkhorn balancing would then be doing the dispersion work.; alpha_l = std(C)/std(B) equalisation can make the behaviour term dominate when the curved cost becomes nearly degenerate, re-introducing instability in exactly the regime it is meant to fix.; The taper keeps the deepest level nearly flat geometrically, so the hyperbolic part of the contribution at level 3 is small and the two-level prefix may carry most of the curvature benefit; the mechanism then rests on the sign inversion plus balancing alone.
ideas.safeguards: Log-domain Sinkhorn with max-subtraction and 30 fixed iterations, eps = 1e-8 on all log and division arguments; column marginals uniform B/K with a guard that K <= B so the problem is feasible; NaN/Inf check after each iteration with fallback to the pure curved-cost argmin for that step; clamp ||r_l|| so sqrt(kappa_l)*||r_l|| <= tanh^{-1}(1 - 1e-6) and clamp s_l to [1e-6, 1e6]; kappa_l recomputed from an EMA so a single bad batch cannot swing the curvature; the negative suffix behaviour term is bounded by alpha_l and standardised per batch so it cannot dominate the curved cost; the level-3 sign inversion is structural (sigma_3 = -1) and its magnitude equalisation is measured per batch, never tuned; straight-through preserves the hard code as the forward value; the behaviour matrices are frozen at evaluation so validation and test cannot update any SID; and hard-ER, positive-hit and l3_collision are recorded as diagnostics only, never used as admission gates.
ideas.spec_equations: Inputs per step: batch of B items, tangent codebooks E_1,E_2,E_3 in R^{256 x d}, EMA scales s_1,s_2,s_3, per-epoch Ab_1,Ab_2,Ab_3 in R^{256x256}, cached succ(i), h_l. 1) r_1(i) = z(i); for l>1: r_l(i) = r_{l-1}(i) - straight_through(E_{l-1}[hard_{l-1}(i)]). 2) s_l <- (1-rho)*s_l + rho*RMS_batch(r_l) with rho = 1/24 (one epoch horizon, documented default). 3) kappa_l = u1^2/(s_1*s_l), u1 = 0.5. 4) u_l(i) = exp_0^{kappa_l}(r_l(i)); c_{l,k} = exp_0^{kappa_l}(E_l[k]). 5) C_l[i,k] = d_{kappa_l}(u_l(i), c_{l,k})^2 / s_l^2. 6) B_l[i,k] = Ab_l[k, h_l(succ(i))]; alpha_l = std(C_l)/std(B_l + eps). 7) M_l = C_l - alpha_l*sigma_l*B_l, sigma = (+1,+1,-1). 8) log-domain Sinkhorn, 30 iterations: f <- log(1) - logsumexp_k(M_l[i,k] + g_k); g <- log(B/K) - logsumexp_i(M_l[i,k] + f_i); P_l = exp(M_l + f + g). 9) hard_l = argmax_k P_l[i,k]; y_l = gather(E_l, hard_l) + (P_l @ E_l - (P_l @ E_l).detach()); decoder input = y_1 + y_2 + y_3; commitment and reconstruction losses in tangent space as in the baseline. 10) every epoch: update h_l from hard codes of all training items and rebuild Ab_l from T and succ; never from validation or test.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Takes: item encoder output z, the three tangent codebooks E_l (256 x d each, trainable), the training-only transition matrix T (sparse, item x item), cached succ(i), an EMA residual-scale vector s in R^3, prior-epoch hard codes h_l, and the batch's residual tensors. Returns: per level a soft assignment P_l (B x 256), a hard code id hard_l (B), the straight-through codeword vector y_l fed to the decoder, and the recorded scalars s_l, kappa_l, u_l, plus the epoch-level code-pair affinity Ab_l and occupancy diagnostics.

specification.text: L=3 levels, K=256 codewords per level, B~1023 items per step (24556/24), tangent codebook parameters E_l in R^{K x d}. Per step and per level l: (i) compute the Euclidean residual r_l(i) from the previous levels' tangent codewords; (ii) update the scalar s_l by EMA over the batch of RMS(r_l); (iii) set kappa_l = u1^2/(s_1*s_l) with the documented default u1 = 0.5 (chosen so the load sqrt(kappa_l)*s_l = u1*sqrt(s_l/s_1) <= 0.5 and artanh stays finite; load decreases with depth because s_l decreases); (iv) map residuals and codewords with the SAME map: u_l(i) = exp_0^{kappa_l}(r_l(i)), c_{l,k} = exp_0^{kappa_l}(E_l[k]); (v) form the normalised curved cost C_l[i,k] = d_{kappa_l}(u_l(i), c_{l,k})^2 / s_l^2; (vi) add the signed per-pair behaviour term sigma_l * alpha_l * Ab_l[k, h_l(succ(i))], sigma_l = +1 for l<3 and -1 for l=3, alpha_l = std_batch(C_l)/std_batch(B_l) (derived equalisation, no tuned weight); (vii) solve log-domain Sinkhorn M_l = C_l - alpha_l*sigma_l*B_l with row marginals 1 and uniform column marginals B/K, T=1 in normalised cost units, 30 fixed iterations; (viii) hard code = argmax_k P_l[i,k], gradient via straight-through y = gather(E_l, hard) + (P_l @ E_l - (P_l @ E_l).detach()). Per epoch, from the codes assigned in the previous epoch and the training-only transition matrix, rebuild h_l (item -> level-l code) and the K x K row-normalised code-pair affinity Ab_l (Ab_l[k,k'] = mass of transitions from items in code k to items whose successor lies in code k'), and pick succ(i) = argmax_j T(i,j) once from the training split. Formula signature: TAPERINNOV(L=3, K=256, u1=0.5, sinkhorn_iters=30, eps=1e-8) -> per level: (s_l, kappa_l, C_l, Ab_l, sigma_l, alpha_l) -> (P_l, hard_l) -> tangent codebook update and decoder input sum_l E_l[hard_l]. Output: three SID digits per item, the same codebook points used for reconstruction, and the recorded diagnostics (s_l, kappa_l, u_l, l3_collision, level-2 distinct prefixes, hard ER, positive-hit rate).

ideas.title: Depth-tapered Poincare curvature with a sign-inverted per-pair behaviour term at the suffix level, dispatched by balanced curved Sinkhorn

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: b_ij:=0 for all pairs, which leaves a pure signed-curvature-ladder RQ (exp/log residual entry, geodesic assignment, sphere deep level) with the behaviour mass absent. The switch exists in the code and is unit-checked, but no arm is trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full mechanism exactly as specified (signed ladder with kappa_0=1/R_bar^2, s_curv=[-1,-1,+1], train-split b_ij, gamma_l frozen from the first batch). This is the ONE candidate that is trained, for 3000 Stage-2 epochs on four cards and then the frozen Stage3 protocol.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: kappa_l:=0 for all l, so exp/log become identity, distances become Euclidean L2 and codewords are plain points, while sigma_l and the behaviour occupancy mass stay active; this isolates what the curvature contributes inside the same coupled score. The switch exists and is unit-checked, no arm is trained.
ideas.behavior_computation: One pass over TRAIN sequences only: n_ij = number of consecutive (i->j) transitions, n_i = sum_j n_ij, T = sum_ij n_ij; then b_ij = clip(log(n_ij*T/(n_i*n_j)), 0, log T)/log T, so 0 means 'no more than chance' (threshold at independence) and 1 means 'maximally over-represented'. Stored as a sparse train-item x train-item table, together with the per-epoch hard SID buffer khat^{prev}_{l,i} produced by forward passes over TRAIN items only.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-transition log-odds (a behaviour-conditioned pair weight), computed over consecutive items of TRAIN sequences and restricted at use time to pairs whose two endpoints are both in the current batch.
ideas.cost_estimate: Same number of forward and backward passes (3000 epochs x 24 steps = 72000 steps), same batch sizes. Extra per step: two exp/log maps and L*K closed-form geodesic-distance evaluations over d-dim vectors (tanh/atanh or tan/arccos, no iteration) plus one sparse scatter over in-batch behaviour pairs (roughly 10-30 neighbours per anchor), i.e. about +5% to +10% wall clock per step. Memory overhead is negligible: occupancy buffer 24556 x 3 x int16 = 0.15 MB plus the sparse train-item b_ij table. No extra epoch, no ablation arm, no sweep, no second seed.
ideas.coupling_equation: score_{l,i,k} = d_{M(kappa_l)}( exp_{kappa_l}(r_{l,i}), exp_{kappa_l}(c_l[k]) ) + sigma_l * gamma_l * sum_{j in N(i)} b_ij * 1[khat_{l,j}^{prev} = k], with sigma_l = s_curv[l] and k_{l,i} = argmin_k score_{l,i,k}.
ideas.coupling_path: A single scalar is the meeting point: the per-level argmin score. The curved geodesic distance defines the geometry of that scalar and the behaviour occupancy mass is added to the same scalar before the argmin, and both are oriented by the same per-level sign table sigma_l=s_curv[l]. Setting b_ij=0 leaves a pure signed-ladder curved RQ (the geometry still chooses every code); setting kappa_l=0 makes the distance and the maps Euclidean while the sigma ladder and the behaviour mass keep acting, so the code path still assigns differently. Removing either changes the actual discrete code selected at every level, not a side loss.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the level-3 collapse was caused by one-sign curvature attracting behaviour-adjacent items into the same deep code, then the sign-flipped deep level plus per-pair repulsion must move l3_collision from the observed 0.549-1.0 down to <=0.35 while keeping valid_l1_hard_er <=4, positive_hit_rate >=0.12 and level2_distinct_prefixes in the thousands, and Stage3 test_recall@10 must exceed 0.065 (baseline 0.0555, best 0.0638). It is falsified if l3_collision stays above 0.5, if valid_l1_hard_er returns to the 16.4 baseline magnitude, or if refinement bits fall below the 2.32 bits measured for OCCURV-FIELD.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the Stage-2 RQ-VAE training loop, jointly in (a) the residual entry exp_{kappa_l}(r_l), (b) the codeword position exp_{kappa_l}(c_l[k]) and its reconstruction log_{kappa_l}, and (c) the geodesic distance that forms the assignment score, at every level l=1..3 with the level-dependent sign and magnitude.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Closed-form exponential and logarithmic maps and geodesic distance of a signed-curvature manifold: Poincare ball of radius 1/sqrt(|kappa_l|) when kappa_l<0, with exp_k(x)=tanh(sqrt(|k|)||x||)/(sqrt(|k|)||x||) * x and d_k(u,v)=(1/sqrt|k|) arcosh(1+2|k||u-v|^2/((1-|k||u|^2)(1-|k||v|^2))); sphere of radius 1/sqrt(kappa_l) when kappa_l>0, with exp_k(x)=tan(sqrt(k)||x||)/(sqrt(k)||x||) * x and d_k(u,v)=(1/sqrt(k)) arccos(clamp(k<u,v>)); identity and L2 when kappa_l=0. Base magnitude kappa_0=1/R_bar^2 from the measured RMS latent norm, ladder kappa_l=s_curv[l]*kappa_0*2^-(l-1) with s_curv=[-1,-1,+1].
ideas.key_change: The RQ assignment at level l becomes argmin_k over a curved geodesic distance on M(kappa_l) (Poincare ball if kappa_l<0, sphere if kappa_l>0) plus sigma_l*gamma_l times the transition-log-odds mass of behaviour neighbours already occupying code k, with the exp/log maps used identically for the residual entry and the codeword positions.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition counts, the b_ij table and the occupancy buffer are built exclusively from TRAIN sequences and TRAIN items; validation interactions are used only after an epoch to log diagnostics and never to build codes, curvatures, gamma_l, R_bar or b_ij; no test interaction of any kind enters SID construction. Cold items get zero rows in b_ij and are quantized by the curved distance alone, so validation or test co-occurrence cannot be smuggled into a prefix.
ideas.motivation: In a 3-level RQ-VAE SID the shallow levels must GROUP behaviour-adjacent items (a shared prefix is what lets the generator name the next item's neighbourhood) while the deepest level must SEPARATE behaviour-confusable items (otherwise the last token cannot disambiguate which successor actually comes next). All three previously run curvature arms used one sign and one strength at every level: they bought level-1 separation (valid_l1_hard_er 2.488-3.885 vs 16.390 baseline, positive_hit_rate 0.0794 -> 0.1222-0.2629) and then destroyed level-3 usage (l3_collision 0.549, 0.943, 1.0), so the SID was rejected by the 35% gate and Stage3 could not benefit.
ideas.novelty: Not holonomy transport, not popularity-derived capacity radii, not a per-occupant curvature field of uniform strength. Here the CURVATURE SIGN ITSELF is a per-level ladder (negative shallow -> positive deepest, magnitude halving per level) and the SAME sign table orients a per-pair behaviour-occupancy term that lives inside the assignment score, so behaviour ATTRACTS on shallow levels and REPELS on the deepest level; the behaviour weight is a train-split transition log-odds thresholded at independence rather than a tuned constant, and the deep level's spreading is structural (sphere + pair repulsion) instead of a usage-balancing loss.
ideas.observables: l3_collision (must fall below 0.35), level2_distinct_prefixes (must stay in the thousands), valid_l1_hard_er (<=4), positive_hit_rate (>=0.12), refinement bits (>=2.3), per-level usage entropy and top-1 codeword share per level, prefix next-item predictability (conditional entropy of the true successor given each prefix length), and Stage3 test_recall@10 as the only judgement (target >0.065).
risks: Repulsion restricted to behaviour neighbours may not de-collide the items with no in-batch neighbour, leaving l3_collision above the 35% gate.; The frozen first-batch median gamma_l can be mis-scaled if the first batch is atypical, making the behaviour term either inert or dominant at level 3.; The sphere level (kappa_3>0) bounds distances, so arccos gradients saturate near-antipodal codewords and can freeze their learning.; The previous-epoch occupancy buffer lags, so an item can be pushed into a code that the next epoch vacates, producing oscillation of level-3 usage.; Even with a clean SID, Stage3 may not convert the gain if the generator's prefix likelihood does not exploit the extra level-3 distinction.
ideas.safeguards: Clamp the ball radius ||u|| <= (1-1e-3)/sqrt(|kappa|) before arcosh; use the series 2*artanh(x)/x -> 2 for small sqrt(|kappa|)||x|| and 2*arctan(x)/x -> 2 for small sqrt(kappa)||x|| so the maps never evaluate 0/0; clamp the arccos argument to [-(1-1e-6), 1-1e-6]; clamp sqrt(kappa)||r|| < pi/(2*sqrt(kappa)) - 1e-3 before tan so sphere points stay inside the chart; guard the Poincare denominator (1-|kappa||u|^2) with 1e-8; freeze gamma_l and R_bar after the first forward pass and mask them from the optimizer; build the occupancy buffer and b_ij under no_grad; skip the behaviour term for anchors with no in-batch neighbour and for cold items; fall back to Euclidean assignment (kappa_l=0) if R_bar is zero or non-finite; keep the straight-through path and the commitment loss in the graph so the encoder cannot collapse to a constant as it did in the holonomy run; log per-level usage entropy every epoch so a level-3 collapse is visible without ever gating on it.
ideas.spec_equations: kappa_0 = 1/R_bar^2 with R_bar = detach(rms_batch(||z||)) computed once and checkpointed; kappa_l = s_curv[l]*kappa_0*2^-(l-1), s_curv=[-1,-1,+1]; b_ij = clip(log(n_ij*T/(n_i*n_j)),0,log T)/log T; gamma_l = detach(median over the first batch of min_k d_{M(kappa_l)}(exp(r_{l,i}),exp(c_l[k]))); u_l = exp_{kappa_l}(r_l); p_lk = exp_{kappa_l}(c_l[k]); score_lk = d_{M(kappa_l)}(u_l,p_lk) + sigma_l*gamma_l*sum_{j in N(i) intersect batch} b_ij*1[khat_{l,j}^{prev}=k]; k_l = argmin_k score_lk; rhat_l = r_l + sg(c_l[k_l]-r_l); r_{l+1} = r_l - c_l[k_l]; L = ||x - Dec(sum_l c_l[k_l])||^2 + beta*sum_l ||r_l - sg(c_l[k_l])||^2 with the baseline beta, and no additional weight on the behaviour term because it acts only through the argmin.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: encoder latent z (width d) for each train item; the L tangent codebooks c_l (K x d); the sparse train-split b_ij table; the previous-epoch SID buffer khat^{prev}. Outputs: one SID per item (k_1,k_2,k_3) with its prefix hierarchy, the per-level quantized tangent vectors c_l[k_l] fed to the decoder and the reconstructed sum used by the decoder, the updated codebooks, the refreshed SID buffer at the end of each epoch, and the stored constants R_bar, kappa_l and gamma_l kept in the checkpoint for exact reproduction.

specification.text: PARAMS: L=3; K=codebook size (baseline 256); d=latent width; tangent codebooks c_l in R^{K x d}; ladder s_curv=[-1,-1,+1]; sigma=s_curv; R_bar=detach(rms over the first training batch of ||z||); kappa_0=1/R_bar^2 (frozen); kappa_l=s_curv[l]*kappa_0*2^-(l-1). BEHAVIOUR (built once, train split only): n_ij=count of consecutive (i->j) transitions; n_i=out mass; T=sum n_ij; b_ij=clip(log(n_ij*T/(n_i*n_j)),0,log T)/log T. FORWARD: z=Enc(x); r_1=z; for l=1..L: u_l=exp_{kappa_l}(r_l); p_lk=exp_{kappa_l}(c_l[k]); dist_lk=d_{kappa_l}(u_l,p_lk); nb_lk=scatter_sum over j in N(i) and in the batch of b_ij*1[khat_{l,j}^{prev}=k]; score_lk=dist_lk+sigma_l*gamma_l*nb_lk; k_l=argmin_k score_lk; rhat_l=r_l+sg(c_l[k_l]-r_l); r_{l+1}=r_l-c_l[k_l]; xhat=Dec(sum_l c_l[k_l]); SID(i)=(k_1,k_2,k_3). gamma_l=frozen median of min_k dist_lk over the first forward batch. Loss = baseline RQ-VAE reconstruction + commitment on c_l[k_l]; the behaviour term exists only inside the argmin, so there is no extra loss weight to tune. Occupancy buffer khat^{prev} from the previous epoch, no_grad, refreshed once per epoch.

ideas.title: Signed per-level curvature ladder with behaviour-oriented pair occupancy: shallow Poincare attraction, deepest-level spherical repulsion, both inside the RQ argmin

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: All neighbourhoods set to empty, hence a_{l,i}=0, qbar = origin, and s_l reduces to the ordinary Poincare geodesic distance to the codeword with the same curvature ladder: a layer-decayed curved RQ with no behaviour. The code path exists and is unit-tested; no arm is trained.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full mechanism: c = (-1,-0.5,0) plus per-item behaviour anchors qbar_{l,i}, giving s_l(i,k) = lambda_{c_l}(qbar) * ||log^{c_l}_{qbar}(p_i) - log^{c_l}_{qbar}(q_k)||. This single run is the only run performed.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: c_l = 0 at every level, so exp and log are the identity/translation, the qbar term cancels exactly in the difference, and s_l becomes ||r_{l,i} - e_{l,k}||_2, i.e. exactly the baseline Euclidean RQ-VAE assignment. The switch exists in code; no arm is trained.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the Stage-2 training interactions only: for each user session every ordered pair (i followed by j within the session window) increments C[i][j]; Cout, Cin and T are the row, column and total sums; pmi(i,j) = log(T*C[i][j]/(Cout[i]*Cin[j]+1)); top-8 j per i by pmi; weights w_ij = pmi_ij^+ / sum_j' pmi_ij'^+, stored as int16 index arrays plus a float weight array of size 24556x8. No validation or test event is read at any point.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item transitions (sequential co-consumption) from the training split, popularity-adjusted by pointwise mutual information, used per neighbour PAIR: each pair (i,j) contributes its weight to item i's base point.
ideas.cost_estimate: Offline graph build once: O(number of transitions) with 24556 items, 8 stored neighbours each, ~200k edges, negligible memory. Per step at the frozen scale (24 steps per epoch, 3000 epochs, B=256, K=256, d=64, L=3): 3*256*8 gathers of 64-d codebook rows (~0.4 MFLOP) plus 3*256*256 pairs of Mobius-and-artanh evaluations (~1e8 flops) = roughly 3-5% of one transformer step; codebook parameters and memory unchanged, extra state is a 3x24556 int16 buffer; no extra epochs.
ideas.coupling_equation: s_l(i,k) = (2/(1 - c_l |qbar_{l,i}|^2)) * || log^{c_l}_{qbar_{l,i}}( exp^{c_l}(r_{l,i}) ) - log^{c_l}_{qbar_{l,i}}( exp^{c_l}(e_{l,k}) ) ||_2, with qbar_{l,i} = exp^{c_l}( sum_{j in N(i)} w_ij * e_{l, z_l(j)} ), z_l(i) = argmin_k s_l(i,k), and c_l = -(L-l)/(L-1).
ideas.coupling_path: behaviour pairs -> weighted mean of neighbour codebook vectors -> base point qbar_{l,i} = exp^{c_l}(a_{l,i}) -> the log map at that base point produces both the residual tangent vector and every codeword tangent vector -> their difference, scaled by the curvature conformal factor, is the assignment score -> argmin selects the level-l codeword -> the residual recursion feeds level l+1. Removing behaviour (qbar=0) changes the score to the plain Poincare geodesic distance; removing curvature (c=0) makes the base point cancel identically so the score is the Euclidean distance; either removal changes the selected codeword and therefore the SID.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: It is worth keeping iff curvature-at-shallow-plus-Euclidean-at-deep retains the first-order gain while restoring level-3 occupancy. Observable: valid_l1_hard_er stays well below the 16.39 baseline and at or under 4, positive_hit_rate at or above 0.12, level2_distinct_prefixes in the thousands rather than 1, l3_collision at or under 0.35, refinement at or above 2.3 bits, and Stage3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 in the single frozen run.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: In the quantiser, at every RQ level: the residual is mapped into the ball by exp^{c_l} before assignment, the codebook is mapped by the same exp^{c_l}, the assignment metric is the curvature-weighted tangent norm at the behaviour base point, and reconstruction decodes the chosen ball position with log^{c_l}. The encoder and decoder are untouched apart from the quantised code they receive.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare-ball exponential and logarithmic maps with fixed negative curvature magnitude per level, c_l = -kappa*(L-l)/(L-1) with kappa=1, i.e. c = (-1.0, -0.5, 0.0), combined with Mobius addition and the conformal factor lambda_c = 2/(1-c|q|^2): exp^c(v) = tanh(sqrt|c||v|)/(sqrt|c||v|) * v, log^c_a(x) = (2/sqrt|c|)*artanh(sqrt|c| |(-a) (+) x|) * ((-a)(+)x)/(sqrt|c| |(-a)(+)x|), whose c->0 limit is the identity/translation.
ideas.key_change: At every RQ level the residual and the codebook are pushed into the Poincare ball by the same curvature-c argument exp^c, and the codeword is chosen by the tangent-space distance measured at a per-item base point qbar, which is the exp^c image of the weighted mean codebook vector of that item's training-only behaviour neighbours. Curvature decreases with depth and is exactly zero at level 3, so the deep assignment is Euclidean while the shallow assignments stay curved and behaviour-specific.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition graph is built before Stage 2 training from training split sequences only; validation and test interactions are never parsed by the SID builder; anchors average codebook vectors of training items only; and the codebooks themselves are fitted on training item content/embeddings only, so no validation or test interaction can influence a SID, an anchor or a codeword position.
ideas.motivation: The three measured curvature arms show that curvature in the RQ assignment buys a real first-order gain (l1 hard ER 2.49-3.89 and positive hit 0.12-0.26 versus baseline 16.39/0.079) but that the same curvature strength at every level funnels the deep residual into a few codewords (l3_collision 0.549 and 0.943), which is why both arms failed the 35% gate. The root cause is geometric: with one fixed chart every item shares the same attractor (the chart centre / the far-boundary region), so residuals of different behaviour groups map to the same level-3 codeword. The fix must keep the curved separation at shallow depth, remove the shared attractor, and end in a genuinely Euclidean deep level.
ideas.novelty: Not holonomy (no two-leg transport), not GEOCAP (no popularity-sizing of codeword radii, no per-codeword capacity), not OCCURV-FIELD (no per-codeword learnable curvature field, and no uniform strength across levels). Here the behaviour signal is a POSITION, not a weight and not a capacity: the directed-transition neighbourhood of each item defines the base point of the exponential/log map used to compare that item's residual with the codebook, and the curvature magnitude is a derived ladder (-1, -0.5, 0) that reaches exactly Euclidean at level 3. There is no mixing coefficient to tune: the only coupling constant is the curvature itself, and it is a fixed unit default with a depth rule derived from L=3.
ideas.observables: valid_l1_hard_er (expect <=4, target 2.5-3.5), positive_hit_rate (expect >=0.12, target >=0.20), level2_distinct_prefixes (expect thousands, not 1 and not 784-with-l3-collapse), l3_collision (must be <=0.35), refinement bits (>=2.3), Stage3 test_recall@10 (>0.065), plus the recorded-only behavioural diagnostics (prefix coherence, behaviour adjacency of SIDs, transfer predictability) which never gate admission.
risks: The lagged assignment buffer can freeze an early bad partition while anchors keep reinforcing it (origin anchors until first sighting mitigates, but a bad first epoch is still possible).; Behaviour neighbours may be too dense or too sparse for some items, so anchors are noisy.; Behaviour-coherent prefixes at levels 1-2 could homogenise the level-3 residual so that even the Euclidean level-3 assignment collides.; If the encoder residual norm collapses, exp^c maps everything near the origin where curvature is locally negligible and the mechanism degrades to baseline.; Single run with no seed repetition: seed noise is part of the uncertainty.
ideas.safeguards: Mobius-addition denominators clamped at 1e-6; artanh arguments clamped to 1-1e-6; ball coordinates clipped to radius 0.95/sqrt|c| (a scale-relative bound derived from the curvature, not a swept constant); c=0 levels take a dedicated Euclidean branch so no division by sqrt|c| can occur at level 3; anchors and the assignment buffer are fully detached (stop-gradient) so no gradient flows through the argmin or across items; buffer entries initialise to -1 giving an origin anchor (deterministic warm-up) and missing neighbours are dropped with weight renormalisation; exp/log evaluated with the clamped forms and a finite-value assertion on s before the argmin, falling back to the Euclidean branch for a batch element if a non-finite score appears; commitment beta, codebook size K, width d, epoch count and the Stage-3 protocol are all inherited unchanged.
ideas.spec_equations: Input item i with encoder output r_1 in R^d; codebooks E_l in R^{K x d}; neighbours (idx_i in Z^8, w_i in R^8). For l = 1..3: c = -(3-l)/2; p = exp_c(r_l); a = sum_{n=1..8} w_i[n] * E_l[ buffer_l[ idx_i[n] ] ] (missing entries skipped, weights renormalised); qbar = exp_c(a); if c>0: qbar = qbar * min(1, 0.95/(sqrt(c)*|qbar|)); for k=0..K-1: q = exp_c(E_l[k]); u_p = log_c(qbar, p); u_q = log_c(qbar, q); s[k] = (2/(1-c*|qbar|^2)) * |u_p - u_q|_2; z_l = argmin_k s[k]; qs = E_l[z_l]; quant_l = qs.detach() + r_l - r_l.detach(); r_{l+1} = r_l - qs; recon_code += quant_l; after the optimiser step buffer_l[i] = z_l. Loss = ||x - Decoder(sum_l quant_l)||^2 + 0.25 * sum_l ||r_l - qs_l||^2 (unchanged baseline losses). SID(i) = (z_1, z_2, z_3).
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: encoder residual r_l (B x d), per-level codebook E_l (K x d), curvature ladder c_l, behavioural neighbour indices and weights (B x 8 each), lagged assignment buffer (3 x 24556). Outputs: hard codes z_l (B,) per level, straight-through quantised vectors quant_l (B x d), updated buffer entries, and the SID tuple per item; the decoder interface is unchanged.

specification.text: 1) Offline, from TRAINING interactions only, build directed transition counts C[i][j] over session windows; score pmi(i,j)=log( T*C[i][j] / (Cout[i]*Cin[j]+alpha) ) with alpha=1, T=total transitions; keep the top m=8 neighbours per item and normalise w_ij. 2) Constants: kappa=1 (unit curvature, documented default), c_l = -kappa*(L-l)/(L-1) for l=1..L, L=3 gives c=(-1,-0.5,0); K and d unchanged from the baseline RQ-VAE; commitment beta=0.25 unchanged. 3) Per step, for each level l: p = exp^{c_l}(r_l) (residual into the ball), q_k = exp^{c_l}(e_{l,k}) (codebook into the SAME ball with the SAME map), anchor a = sum_j w_ij * ehat_{l,z_j} using a lagged hard-assignment buffer, qbar = exp^{c_l}(a), then z_l = argmin_k (2/(1-c_l|qbar|^2)) * ||log^{c_l}_{qbar}(p) - log^{c_l}_{qbar}(q_k)||. 4) r_{l+1} = r_l - e_{l,z_l}; reconstruction uses the same ball positions decoded by log^{c_l} (which returns e_{l,z_l}); straight-through quant_l = e_{l,z_l}.detach() + r_l - r_l.detach(). 5) Buffer A[l,i] is updated after each optimiser step with the current z_l(i); unseen entries hold -1, i.e. origin anchor, which is the deterministic epoch-1 warm-up (no schedule to tune).

ideas.title: Behaviour-anchored, depth-decayed curvature: each item's residual is quantised in the Poincare chart centred on its own behaviour neighbourhood, with curvature falling to exactly Euclidean at level 3.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: USE_BEHAVIOUR=False: b_i term deleted, cost reduces to d_(kappa_l)(u_i,e_c)^2/a_l^2 only, no successor table is read; curvature schedule and Sinkhorn unchanged. Present and correct in code, never trained.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The single trained candidate: per-layer decaying kappa_l, geodesic cost plus Karcher-mean behaviour term, Sinkhorn with uniform column marginal and plan-based straight-through, baseline reconstruction and commitment losses. One run, one seed, no early stopping.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: USE_HYPERBOLIC=False: kappa_l = 0, exp_0 and log_p become identity, d becomes Euclidean ||.||/a_l, the Karcher mean becomes the weighted arithmetic mean, and the same Sinkhorn runs on Euclidean squared distances; behaviour term unchanged. Present and correct in code, never trained.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training split only: for each item i count directed transitions i->j inside the training sequences, keep the top M=8 successors by count as Succ(i) with weights w_ij equal to those counts. Once per epoch, record every training item's hard codeword at each layer T_l[i] from that epoch's forward pass; the next epoch consumes the previous table. No other statistic is used.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item transitions (sequential co-consumption) carried per item-successor pair as integer weights w_ij, together with each successor's previous-epoch hard codeword at the same layer.
ideas.cost_estimate: Stage 2 only. Per step (B~1024 residuals, K codewords per level, L=3, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs = 72000 steps) the mechanism adds 3*B*K geodesic terms (about 0.79M at K=256, 3.1M at K=1024), 3 Karcher means of 8 neighbours and 16 log-domain Sinkhorn sweeps on 3 matrices of size B x K: roughly +10 to +18 percent step time and a few MB of activation memory. The successor code table is 24556 x 3 bytes; curvature statistics are one percentile per layer per epoch.
ideas.coupling_equation: C_ic = [d_(kappa_l)(exp_0^{kappa_l}(r_i^l), e_c)]^2 / a_l^2 + [d_(kappa_l)(e_c, Frechet_{kappa_l}({e_{T_l[j]} : j in Succ(i), w_ij}))]^2 / a_l^2 ; P = Sinkhorn(C/eps_l, rows 1/B, cols 1/K) ; c_i = argmax_c P_ic ; z_i^l = e_{c_i} + (sum_c P_ic e_c - sg(sum_c P_ic e_c)) ; where the behaviour term is the Karcher-mean successor code centroid b_i and the curved term is d_(kappa_l) with kappa_l = -1/a_l^2.
ideas.coupling_path: One cost matrix per layer, C_ic = d_(kappa_l)(u_i,e_c)^2/a_l^2 + d_(kappa_l)(e_c,b_i^l)^2/a_l^2 with b_i^l the Karcher mean of the successor codewords, feeds a Sinkhorn plan whose argmax assigns the code and whose soft form carries the gradient. Removing behaviour removes b_i and changes the cost and the gradient; removing curvature changes the distances, the exp/log maps, the Karcher mean and the layer schedule; dropping either leaves a different core computation.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If level-3 collapse is caused by curvature at depth rather than by the RQ residual itself, then per-layer curvature decaying with remaining residual mass plus a balanced transport marginal must keep valid_l1_hard_er <= 4 and positive_hit_rate >= 0.12 while pushing l3_collision under 0.35, level2_distinct_prefixes above 4000 and refinement near 2.8 bits, and that configuration is what can move Stage3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 (baseline 0.0555, historical best 0.0638). Observe per-layer codeword usage entropy: it should be flat across the three layers instead of collapsing at level 3.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the layer-l RQ quantisation step of Stage 2 (assignment cost, behaviour target and reconstruction), separately at each of the L=3 residual levels, with the same curvature and the same codeword positions used for assignment and for reconstruction.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare-ball geodesic distance d_(kappa_l) with an explicit per-layer negative curvature kappa_l = -1/a_l^2 (a_l = q_l * S_1/S_l derived from measured residual scales), its exponential map exp_0 used to inject each residual into the ball, its logarithmic map log_p used inside the Karcher mean, and the same curvature used for assignment and reconstruction. |kappa_l| decreases with depth and layer 3 is nearly flat yet still evaluated through the curved map.
ideas.key_change: The layer-l RQ assignment becomes the argmax of a Sinkhorn plan on a curvature-normalised geodesic cost matrix augmented with the geodesic distance from each codeword to the hyperbolic centroid of the item's training-successor codewords; reconstruction keeps the hard codeword in the forward pass and takes encoder and codebook gradients through the plan.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Successor lists, successor weights and the codeword table T_l come exclusively from training-split sequences and from encoder forward passes on training batches. Validation and test interactions are never read, cached or used in the codebook, the curvature radii, the transport marginals or the successor targets, so no validation or test interaction can enter SID construction.
ideas.motivation: RQ-VAE SIDs are assigned by nearest-codeword under a flat metric, so an item and its habitual successors land in unrelated prefixes and the deepest level saturates on a few codewords, capping Stage3 next-item recall. Curvature fixed level-1 separation but crushed level 3, because deep residuals are small and sit exactly where the curved metric distorts most. The mechanism therefore needs curvature that literally decays with depth plus a spreading force at depth that is behavioural rather than geometric.
ideas.novelty: None of the three prior curvature arms used a transport plan. Here the assignment itself is a doubly-stochastic entropic optimal-transport plan: the ground cost is a per-layer Poincare geodesic distance whose curvature radius is tied to that layer's remaining residual mass (so curvature decays layer by layer and level 3 is nearly Euclidean), the cost carries a second term to the Karcher mean of the item's training-successor codewords (per-pair behaviour), the column marginal is uniform (the explicit deep-layer spreading force that the collapsed arms lacked), and the straight-through path is the plan itself. No path transport (holonomy), no popularity-derived per-codeword radii (GEOCAP), no per-codeword curvature field uniform across layers (OCCURV-FIELD).
ideas.observables: valid_l1_hard_er (expect <= 4), positive_hit_rate (expect >= 0.12), level2_distinct_prefixes (expect > 4000), l3_collision (expect <= 0.35), refinement bits (expect ~2.8), per-layer codeword usage entropy (expect flat instead of collapsing at level 3), the transport plan's column-marginal residual, and Stage3 test_recall@10 as the sole judgement.
risks: RQ residual mass may not decay enough for a_l and kappa_l to separate the layers, leaving level 3 curved and collapsing again.; The epoch-lagged successor code table can oscillate or stall early while assignments are still moving.; Column-uniform Sinkhorn balancing can fight per-item identity and raise level-1 hard ER above the 4 target.; Items with no training successor drop the behaviour term and dilute the coupling.; Per-layer percentiles are noisy at the start of training before the residual scale settles.; Behavioural successor coherence can merge prefixes of consecutive items and lose discriminability the generator needs.
ideas.safeguards: Log-domain Sinkhorn with the cost clamped at 1e3*eps_l; eps_l floored at 1e-8 and rescaled when a row has near-equal costs; Taylor branch for exp_0 when ||v|| < 1e-6; artanh argument clamped to 1-1e-7; a_l floored at 1e-3 and |kappa_l| capped at 1e-4 so the near-Euclidean deep layer never divides by zero; q_l falls back to the running value when an epoch has fewer than 100 residuals at that layer; items with empty Succ(i) get the behaviour term dropped for that row; T_l refreshed only at epoch boundaries and always detached from the graph; successor lists and the codeword table receive no gradient.
ideas.spec_equations: (1) Per epoch, from training batches: q_l = 90th percentile of ||r_i^l||, S_l = mean_i sum_{m>=l} ||r_i^m||, a_l = q_l * S_1 / S_l, kappa_l = -1/a_l^2. (2) exp_0^{kappa}(v) = tanh(sqrt(|kappa|)||v||/2) * v / (sqrt(|kappa|)||v||). (3) d_(kappa)(p,q) = (2/sqrt(|kappa|)) * artanh( sqrt(|kappa|) * ||(-p) xor q|| / sqrt((1-|kappa||p|^2)(1-|kappa||q|^2)) ), divided by a_l for scale-free costs. (4) Karcher: p <- e_{T[j*]} with j* the most frequent successor; repeat 3 times: p <- exp_p( sum_j w_ij log_p(e_{T[j]}) / sum_j w_ij ). (5) C_ic = d_(kappa_l)(u_i,e_c)^2/a_l^2 + d_(kappa_l)(e_c,b_i)^2/a_l^2. (6) eps_l = mean_i min_c C_ic; P = 16-iteration log-domain Sinkhorn with marginals 1/B and 1/K. (7) c_i = argmax_c P_ic (lowest index on ties); z_i^l = e_{c_i} + (sum_c P_ic e_c - sg(sum_c P_ic e_c)); r_i^{l+1} = r_i^l - z_i^l. (8) Losses unchanged from the baseline RQ-VAE; no extra loss term.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: layer-l residual matrix R (B x d) from the frozen encoder and the previous levels, codebook E_l (K x d), the training-split successor lists and weights, the previous-epoch codeword table T_l, the previous-epoch scalars q_l and S_l. Outputs: hard code indices c_i, quantised vector z_i^l whose forward value equals e_{c_i}, next residual r_i^{l+1}, the plan P (detached after use), and refreshed q_l, S_l and T_l at epoch end.

specification.text: Per layer l in 1..3, per training step: build residual matrix R (B x d) from the frozen encoder/previous levels; map each residual into the Poincare ball with exp_0 under curvature kappa_l = -1/a_l^2 where a_l = q_l * S_1/S_l from last epoch's measured 90th-percentile residual norm q_l and mean remaining residual mass S_l; build cost C_ic = d_(kappa_l)(u_i,e_c)^2/a_l^2 + d_(kappa_l)(e_c,b_i)^2/a_l^2 with b_i the 3-step Karcher mean of the successor codewords taken from the previous-epoch hard-code table; compute P = Sinkhorn(C/eps_l) with eps_l = mean_i min_c C_ic, 16 log-domain iterations, marginals 1/B and 1/K; assign c_i = argmax_c P_ic; quantise with z_i^l = e_{c_i} + (sum_c P_ic e_c - sg(sum_c P_ic e_c)); next residual r_i^{l+1} = r_i^l - z_i^l; baseline reconstruction and commitment losses unchanged, no new loss term. Switches USE_BEHAVIOUR and USE_HYPERBOLIC exist and are correct; only both-on is trained.

ideas.title: Stratified-curvature, behaviour-marginal hyperbolic Sinkhorn assignment for RQ-VAE Semantic IDs

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: tau_l=0 for all layers, i.e. the pure layer-ramped curved-metric capacity-balanced assignment (config flag exists, not trained this round).
ideas.ablation_both_on: the full coupled run, kappa=[kappa0,kappa0/2,0] with behaviour attraction at layers 1-2, branch repulsion at layer 3 and capacity-balanced layer 3; the only arm trained.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: kappa0=0 so kappa_l=0 everywhere, exp/log become identity and d_kappa becomes Euclidean while behaviour masses, sign schedule, capacity and straight-through path stay unchanged (flag exists, not trained).
ideas.behavior_computation: From training sequences only: N(a->b)=count of consecutive (a,b) pairs; row-stochastic w(a,b)=N(a->b)/sum_b' N(a->b). Complement mass A_l(i,j)=sum_{n in Top50(i) by w(i,.)} w(i,n)*1[pi_l(n)=j]. Branch mass: Pred(i)=top 10 predecessors by N(s->i); for pairs (i,n) with N(i->n)+N(n->i)=0, b(i,n)=sum_{s in Pred(i) cap Pred(n)} min(w(s,i),w(s,n)); keep top 16 by b, normalise so sum_n b(i,n)=1; R_l(i,j)=sum_n b(i,n)*1[pi_l(n)=j]; pi_l = stop-gradient EMA (eta=1e-3) of the model's own hard training assignments.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-to-item transitions (next-item co-consumption) and user-interest branching (items sharing a predecessor set but not linked by a transition), as per-(item,codeword) masses from the Stage-2 training split only.
ideas.cost_estimate: One run, 3000 Stage-2 epochs x 24 steps x B=1024 over 24556 training items; no extra forward pass and no new loss weight. Per step over the baseline quantizer: exp/log on B+K vectors per layer (negligible), the 3-layer curved distance at the same B*K*d FLOP count (~25M MAC), one 3-iteration Sinkhorn at layer 3 (3*B*K=0.8M) and one B*K sort (0.26M elements, ~1-3 ms GPU): roughly +3% to +6% wall-clock per step (~1.05x the frozen budget). One-off CPU precompute of sparse transition/branch tables (~0.5M entries, minutes).
ideas.coupling_equation: C_ij^(l) = d_{kappa_l}(exp_0^{kappa_l}(r_i), exp_0^{kappa_l}(c_j))^2 - s_l*tau_l*clip(B_l(i,j)/mean_j B_l(i,j), -3, +3), with kappa=[kappa0,kappa0/2,0], s=[+1,+1,-1], B_l=A_l for l<=2 and R_l for l=3, tau_l=0.1*mean_ij m_ij^(l).
ideas.coupling_path: One cost matrix per layer whose metric is the curved distance and whose additive term is that same layer's behaviour mass; the argmin (or capacitated transport argmax at layer 3) of that single matrix picks the codeword, the codeword sets the next residual, and the prefix statistics pi_l through which the behaviour mass is gathered are the model's own curved decisions; tau=0 changes which code wins and kappa0=0 changes the metric inside the same expression.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis:
If deep collapse (not curvature in general) is the blocker, then kappa_3=0 plus layer-3 branch repulsion plus cap=4 per codeword drops l3_collision from 0.549/0.943 to below 0.35 while valid_l1_hard_er stays <=4 and positive_hit_rate >

=0.12, keeping refinement >=2.3 bits and level2_distinct_prefixes >=4000, and Stage3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.0638 with >0.065 the target. Falsified if l3_collision stays >0.35, or ER >4, or hit rate <0.12, or test_R@10 <=0.0638.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ quantization itself, at the assignment step of every layer, and through the scale-matched commit term in the codebook parameter update; the layer-3 residual is the residual of curved layers 1-2, so curvature still reaches layer 3 through the residual chain although its own metric is flat.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Fixed negative curvature per layer kappa_l in {kappa0, kappa0/2, 0}, kappa0=1/median||z-mean||^2; the operations are exp_0^kappa(v)=tanh(sqrt(kappa)||v||)/(sqrt(kappa)||v||)*v, its inverse log map, and the Poincare distance d_kappa(u,v)=(1/sqrt(kappa))*arcosh(1+2*kappa*||u-v||^2/((1-kappa*||u||^2)(1-kappa*||v||^2))); at kappa_3=0 they reduce to identity and the Euclidean norm.
ideas.key_change: The residual and the codebook of layer l both pass through the same exponential map exp_0^{kappa_l} into one Poincare chart with curvature [kappa0, kappa0/2, 0]; squared Poincare distance minus a scaled per-(item,codeword) behaviour mass is the cost; the code is that cost's argmin at layers 1-2 and a capacitated transport argmax at layer 3; straight-through and tangent-space reconstruction are preserved.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Both tables are built once at step 0 from the Stage-2 training split only (asserted on the split name, hard failure otherwise); pi_l is an EMA of assignments produced on training mini-batches. Validation/test interactions are never read, counted, or fed into any SID, cost, curvature, capacity or codebook; the validation split enters only post-hoc diagnostic reporting after the epoch SIDs are frozen.
ideas.motivation: Curvature in the first RQ layer buys the first-order gain (valid_l1_hard_er 16.39 -> 2.49/3.89, positive_hit_rate 0.079 -> 0.12/0.26) but the same uniform curvature at every layer crushes the deepest codebook (l3_collision 0.549 and 0.943), blocking the 35% gate and therefore Stage3. The needed asymmetry: coarse SIDs pulled together by co-consumption so prefixes are predictable, fine SIDs pushed apart so substitutable next items stay distinguishable and the deep codebook stays occupied.
ideas.novelty: Curvature is a LAYER RAMP reaching exactly zero at the deepest RQ layer and the behaviour term flips sign with depth (complement/transition attraction at layers 1-2, branch-alternative repulsion at layer 3), both inside the SAME cost matrix that drives assignment; the deepest layer also gets an explicit capacity (each codeword used ceil(B/K) times) so occupancy cannot collapse by construction. It is not cross-chart holonomy transport, not popularity-derived area-law radii, not per-codeword reach curvature at uniform intensity.
ideas.observables:
l3_collision below 0.35 (was 0.549/0.943/1.0); per-layer usage entropy near log 256 at layer 3 (capacity forces 4 it

ems per codeword per batch); valid_l1_hard_er <=4 and not back in the 16.39 band; positive_hit_rate >=0.12; refinement >=2.3 bits; level2_distinct_prefixes >=4000; per-layer codebook gradient norms and row-wise commit distances shift with the ramp; final Stage3 test_recall@10 above 0.065.
risks: Capacity balancing may force semantically poor layer-3 codes and push hard ER above 4 (main risk); shallow complement attraction may re-inflate level-1/2 collisions and undo the curvature gain; the EMA prefix table lags early so the behaviour cost is noise for hundreds of steps; sparse predecessor counts are head-item dominated so repulsion may concentrate on popular items; the B*K sort adds a small sync per step; single-seed noise of a few 1e-3 on recall could hide a small real gain.
ideas.safeguards: assert B>=K and cap>=1; kappa_l>=0 with an exact Euclidean branch at kappa_l=0 (limit forms) so layer 3 never divides by zero; clamp ball norm to (1-1e-5)/sqrt(kappa) so tanh saturation cannot zero the distance denominator; floor distance denominators at 1e-6; log-domain Sinkhorn with row-max subtraction and fixed 3 iterations, eps_3 floored at 1e-6; all buffer statistics detached; tau=0 for the first 50 steps and while the prefix EMA is cold; a non-finite guard replacing a non-finite cost row by the Euclidean distance row with a logged counter; deterministic stable double-key sort in the capacity greedy; behaviour-table build asserts the training split name and fails hard otherwise; no validation/test data read inside any of these paths.
ideas.spec_equations: kappa0=1/median_b||z_b-mean(z)||^2 (step 0, detached); kappa_l=kappa0*(3-l)/2; exp0^k(v)=tanh(sqrt(k)||v||)/(sqrt(k)||v||+1e-12)*v (identity if k=0); dk(u,v) as above (||u-v||^2 if k=0); m_ij^l=dk(Rt_i,Ct_j)^2; uhat=clip(B_l(i,j)/(mean_j B_l(i,j)+1e-8),-3,3).detach(); C_ij^l=m_ij^l-s_l*tau_l*uhat; k_i=argmin_j C_ij^l for l<3; for l=3: K_ij=exp(-C_ij/eps_3), log-domain Sinkhorn T=3 with row marginal 1/B and column marginal 1/K, then order pairs by (C_ij,-log P_ij) ascending and greedily assign with remaining capacity cap=ceil(B/K); q_i=C_l[k_i]; r_{l+1}=r_l+(q_i-r_l).detach(); L_tot=||x-Dec(sum_l q^{(l)})||^2+sum_l[||sg(r_l)-q^{(l)}||^2+0.25*||r_l-sg(q^{(l)})||^2+commit_l], commit_l=0.25*dk(Rt_l,Ct_{k})^2 if kappa_l>0 else ||sg(r_l)-q||^2.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: encoder latents z in R^{B x d} (B=1024), codebooks C_1..C_3 in R^{256 x d}, frozen kappa0, per-step eps_3 and tau_l, behaviour masses A_l/R_l gathered for the batch from the training-only sparse tables and the stop-gradient prefix EMA pi_l, and reconstruction target x. Outputs: hard code indices k_1,k_2,k_3 per item (the SIDs consumed by Stage 3), the tangent quantized vector z_q=sum_l C_l[k_l] for the decoder, per-layer commit values for the codebook update, and diagnostics (usage histogram, entropy, collision/prefix counts).

specification.text:
L=3 codebooks C_l in R^{256 x d} (K=256, d=encoder width, not swept); frozen kappa0=1/median_b||z_b-mean(z)||^2 from step 0; kappa_l=kappa0*(L-l)/(L-1) -> [k0,k0/2,0]; eps_l=median_{i,j}m_ij^l and tau_l=0.1*mean_{i,j}m_ij^l (per step, detached); beta=0.25; eta=1e-3; T=3 Sinkhorn iterations; 50-step behaviour warmup with tau=0; cap=ceil(B/K)=4.
Per step: r=z=Enc(x) [B=1024,d]; for l=1..3: Rt=exp0^{kappa_l}(r), Ct=exp0^{kappa_l}(C_l), m_ij=dkappa_l(Rt_i,Ct_j)^2; B_l=A_l (l<=2) or R_l (l=3); uhat=detach(clip(B_l(i,j)/(mean_j B_l(i,j)+1e-8),-3,3)); C_ij=m_ij-s_l*tau_l*uhat with s=[+1,+1,-1]; l<3: k_i=argmin_j C_ij; l=3: P=log-domain Sinkhorn(-C/eps_3, rows 1/B, cols 1/K, T=3), then capacitated greedy over ascending (C_ij,-log P_ij) with cap=4; q_i=C_l[k_i]; commit_l=0.25*dkappa_l(sg[Rt_i],Ct_{k_i})^2 if kappa_l>0 else ||sg[r_i]-C_l[k_i]||^2; r <- r+(q_i-r).detach(); z_q=sum_l q_l; L_tot=||x-Dec(z_q)||^2+sum_l[||sg[r_l]-C_l[k]||^2+beta*||r_l-sg[C_l[k]]||^2+commit_l].

papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.

papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.

Read: the five proposal blocks and every frozen evidence bundle (5be6b69ef273217d TAPERINNOV, 7a9fa7a004faa023 signcurv, 25a10c7ce355fe88 ANCHORLADDER, 6f84072b9a4095d4 strataot, a674de47566b29d6 dualramp); all bundles share the same E4-E13 evidence and differ only in the PROPOSED rows (E1/E2/E3/E12/E13). Still open: which proposal the evidence actually supports, and the internal inconsistencies about l3_collision.

STEP 2 — Goal: pin down what the frozen evidence can and cannot say about the failure mode all five proposals are built to fix. Read: E6 (width-20 beam survival) and E7 (teacher-forced per-position NLL), plus E5, E8, E11 and the shared E10 graph statistics. Observed: the strongest discrimination in the bundle is between the uniform-curvature arm l1_br (recall@10 0.04671, gold prefix alive at depth 1/2/3/4 = 1.000/1.000/1.000/0.068, T4 NLL 9.03) and its Euclidean twin l1_br_euclid (0.06207, 1.000/0.829/0.161/0.085, T4 NLL 1.23) and l1_only (0.06233, 0.161/0.086, 1.19) — i.e. curvature/behaviour override held all the way to depth does crush the deepest digit, and dropping it at depth recovers depth-3 survival and ~+0.016 recall. E5 gives the behavioural asymmetry (top-1 successor mass 0.4375 in the lowest-entropy quintile vs 0.0543 in the highest, Spearman -0.973), E8 gives the capacity fact (K=16 co-clusters 0.3106 of canonical pairs, K=256 only 0.0822, negatives 0.1352/0.0129), E11 shows baseline first-prefix sharing barely above the permutation null (0.0907 vs 0.067). Open: final ordering.

STEP 3 — Goal: discriminate the five on coupling quality, derived-constant discipline and transfer of their spreading device to the single run.
